case.case_title: Jayakody v. Karunanayake, Officer-in-Charge, Police Station, Polgahawela and Attorney-General
case.source_citation: Sri Lanka Law Reports [1994] 2 Sri LR 264

clause.text: All persons are equal before the law and are entitled to the equal protection of the law.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner’s rights under Article 12(1) were infringed by alleged discriminatory treatment during the 1991 Local Authorities Elections campaign and arrest.
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed that he was obstructed in his election campaign and arrested without warrant for a non-cognizable offence, while other political groups campaigned freely, thus infringing his rights under Article 12(1).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondent argued that the petitioner was not entitled to the same rights as the de jure leader of the Independent Group since he was only a strong supporter and de facto leader, and that the arrest was lawful based on information received about transporting voters.
key_facts: Petitioner was a former MP who supported the Independent Group in 1991 elections but was not a candidate or official leader.
Petitioner was arrested without warrant on polling day for alleged transport of voters, a non-cognizable offence under s. 81C of the Local Authorities Elections Ordinance.
Other political party members campaigned freely while petitioner’s campaign was obstructed.
Petitioner claimed discrimination and infringement of fundamental rights under Articles 12(1), 12(2), 13(1), and 14(1)(c).
Court found petitioner’s arrest unlawful but did not find infringement of Articles 12 and 14(1)(c) rights.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: The court interpreted Article 12(1) as guaranteeing equality before the law and equal protection, but clarified that the petitioner, as a de facto leader and not the official leader or candidate, was not entitled to the same rights and privileges as the de jure leader of the group.
reasoning.application_to_facts: The court found that the petitioner was not similarly circumstanced as recognized political party leaders and that his claim to equal treatment was not established. The petitioner’s arrest was unlawful under Article 13(1), but no infringement of Article 12(1) was found because the petitioner’s status did not entitle him to special protection beyond that of an ordinary supporter.
principles_established: Article 12(1) guarantees equality before the law and equal protection but does not extend special rights to de facto leaders beyond those of ordinary supporters.
Discriminatory treatment claims under Article 12(1) require the claimant to be similarly circumstanced to those allegedly favored.
Unlawful arrest under Article 13(1) does not automatically imply infringement of Article 12(1) rights.

outcome.holding: The court held that the petitioner’s rights under Article 12(1) were not infringed.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 12(1) was central to the petitioner’s claim of discrimination in election campaign treatment and arrest, but the court found no infringement because the petitioner was not entitled to the same legal protections as the official group leader.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The court found that the petitioner was a de facto leader but not entitled to the same rights as the de jure leader, and that the alleged infringements of Articles 12 and 14(1)(c) were not established.
